title: Breast biopsy
what: Using ultrasound to guide it, the doctor takes tiny pieces of breast tissue with a thin needle. They are studied under a microscope.
why: When an ultrasound or mammogram found a lump or spot, and it needs to be known exactly what it is.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes; taking the samples takes a few minutes
tell_doctor: Blood thinners. The doctor will tell you if you need to stop them

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually you can eat as normal. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: On the day of the procedure, do not put cream on your breasts or deodorant under your arms.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes with a top that is easy to take off. A firm bra will support the breast afterwards.

bring: Your ultrasound and mammogram images and reports
steps: You lie on your back or slightly on your side
The doctor finds the right spot with ultrasound
The skin is cleaned and you get a numbing injection
A tiny nick is made in the skin
Several samples are taken with the needle. You will hear a click
Sometimes a tiny marker is left to mark the spot
The spot is pressed and covered with a bandage
feel: The numbing injection burns a little
Then you feel pressure and clicks, but not pain
If it hurts, tell the doctor. You will get more numbing
after: A cold pack on the breast, through cloth, reduces swelling and bruising
A bruise and soreness for a few days are normal
No sports or heavy lifting for 1 to 2 days
Results usually come in 1 to 2 weeks. The doctor explains them
red_flags: The bandage soaks through with blood, or the breast swells fast
Fever, redness, or strong pain that gets worse

faq.a: It is done with local numbing. Usually you feel only the injection and pressure.

faq.q: Can a biopsy cause harm if the lump is dangerous?
faq.a: No. Current evidence shows a biopsy does not speed up or spread the disease. Without it, the right treatment cannot be chosen.

faq.q: Why is a marker left in the breast?
faq.a: So the spot can be found exactly later. The marker is tiny, safe, and does not affect MRI.

reminders.text: Biopsy tomorrow. Bring your ultrasound and mammogram images. Do not put on cream or deodorant.
